stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Live Preview across GO, UP, MX platforms in a CMS is a complex feature requiring real-time content rendering, state synchronization, and multi-platform considerations. openspec needed first to elaborate requirements and propose AC; speckit then to harden testability, security (preview endpoint exposure), and edge cases (connection drops, stale previews, concurrent edits).

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Contentstack Live Preview integration. The central attachment point is useContent (236 callers), the single hook through which all content flows. Live Preview SDK configuration and event subscription must plug into or alongside this hook/provider so that every consumer automatically receives preview content without individual component changes. No acceptance criteria were provided; VCs derived from the description alone.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with valuable context: useContent is the central hook (236 callers) and the integration must be transparent to consumers. I built the full AC list from that context. Caveat: I could not read the actual file contents of useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, ContentstackImage.tsx, or contentCard.ts — those files may reveal additional integration points, existing patterns, or constraints that would refine these criteria further. AC-1/AC-2 cover core Live Preview behavior. AC-3 ensures backward compatibility. AC-4 gates Live Preview to non-production. AC-5 handles SDK failure gracefully. AC-6/AC-7 verify the two named components work with preview content. AC-8 is the key 'no consumer code changes' criterion from openspec's notes. AC-9/AC-10/AC-11 cover edge cases (session end, concurrent edits, rapid edits). AC-12 ensures the service layer is covered, not just the hook. AC-13 prevents the SDK from blocking initial render.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Openspec identified the critical architectural anchor (useContent hook, 236 callers, consumer transparency requirement) but failed to produce acceptance criteria — its primary deliverable for a greenfield story with empty AC. Speckit compensated by building 13 ACs from openspec's contextual notes, covering core behavior, backward compatibility, environment gating, failure handling, edge cases, and the no-consumer-changes criterion. Value was complementary but asymmetric: openspec provided strategy, speckit did the heavy spec lifting. Speckit also flagged it could not read key source files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, ContentstackImage.tsx, contentCard.ts), meaning the 13 ACs may miss existing patterns or integration points. A human should verify the ACs against the actual codebase and confirm openspec's architectural assumptions hold.
